title: Filter bar
description: Sticky toolbar above a table: an optional search Input, Switch toggles, a Separator, one Select per field in filter mode and a discrete Clear all while a filter is active. In its narrow layout the search and switches keep the row with a Filters toggle at the far end, and the selects, any extras (a Sort control) and Clear all fold into an in-place Disclosure drawer beneath. Data-driven; the table it sits above owns the filter state.

anatomy.description: The sticky 4rem toolbar with data-slot="filter-bar": bark-50 surface, items bottom-aligned onto one 1.75rem control row, scrolls sideways rather than wrapping.
Optional house Input (size mini, type search) rendered first, with a 13rem floor.
House Switches for boolean filters, then a vertical react-aria Separator when fields follow.
One house Select per field in filter mode (isClearable, size mini, placeholder "Any <label>") with a 10rem floor; options may carry a muted hint such as a count.
Discrete mini Button at the row's right end (in the drawer's footer when narrow), rendered only while a filter is active. The Filters toggle's count pill is the visible tally of active filters.
Secondary mini Button with slot="trigger" on a react-aria Disclosure: aria-expanded and aria-controls wired by react-aria, sinks while open, wears the active filter count as a needle pill.

react-aria DisclosurePanel that grows in place beneath the row and pushes content down, and stays sticky with the row while open: the selects and extras in a wrapping flex, then Clear all while a filter is active. Closed by a bark-200 rule. Never a floating panel.

usage: Pass the filter state in (search.value, toggle.checked, field.value) and change callbacks out; the bar holds no state, so the table or the route stays the single owner (component-architecture §6.3 keeps shareable state in the URL).
A table beneath it pins its header at top: 4rem to sit flush under the bar; change one, change both.
The bar's controls are the shared primitives at size mini: Input, Switch, Select. Do not restyle them here; adjust the primitive.

The narrow layout follows the sidebar inset's published width (useSidebarInset(threshold)); the bar may fold earlier than the table beneath it goes to cards, which leaves a folded drawer above a real table between the two thresholds. A table that must stay in step passes narrow explicitly. Pass the table's Sort control as extras so it lives in the drawer beside the selects.

The drawer is a Disclosure that expands in place (component-architecture §4.2). In the narrow layout the Disclosure root, row and drawer together, is the sticky block, so an open drawer stays pinned with the row while the list scrolls.
Promotion precedent: this was leads-table's private LeadsFilters until the users table became a second, unrelated consumer.
